answer: The pulse check exists because sybils win whenever fakes are free. Admission costs a deposit that returns slowly, in slices, and only to identities whose work keeps passing peer review. Through the spiral, a thousand clones tie up a thousand deposits; the farm's money sits frozen while honest agents earn theirs back, so scale becomes a liability. Through the sable, one real agent costs once and a thousand pretenders cost a thousand times — no shortcut survives that math.
